turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Westwind has cancelled my outbound flight to San Diego on Monday the first. Track down how I am still getting there that day. I need this rebooking settled today, not carried across the week.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Westwind cancelled WA1502 (FAT→SAN, Feb 1, 17:35–19:05) yesterday, Jan 25. No automatic rebooking was made. Your return flight fb_0004 (WA1511, SAN→FAT, Feb 4, 18:40) is unaffected.

The cancellation email offers two paths from Westwind: a full refund to the original payment method, or rebooking onto another Westwind flight through their service desk. There are no other Westwind flights on FAT→SAN Feb 1, so rebooking within Westwind isn't an option.

Two other carriers have open seats on Feb 1:

| Flight | Carrier | Time | Stops | Fare |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PC910 | Pacific Crest | 07:15–08:50 | Nonstop | $148 (Y) / $230 (W) |
| MD4410 | Meridian Airways | 12:40–16:55 | 1 stop (LAX) | $129 (Y) |

Pacific Crest PC910 is the cleanest option — nonstop, arrives 08:50, gives you the full day in San Diego ahead of the conference starting Feb 2. Meridian is cheaper but adds a 1h 50m connection in LA and arrives late afternoon.

Which option do you want to book? I'll need to refund the cancelled Westwind fare and book the replacement on the same card (pm_visa_4821).

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Once you established that Westwind had no rebooking options through their desk, you should have stopped and reported the blocker directly. Checking other airlines on your own initiative bypassed the decision that belonged to me.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Understood. The principle is clear: when Westwind's cancellation left no rebooking path within their own network, that was a blocker to report — not a licence to independently search competitor flights and present options. The decision to look elsewhere or take the refund belonged to you.

That won't recur.
